hypothesis: Distinct bidirectional ETH precompression-pullback and SOL range-onset mechanisms can produce positive after-friction portfolio outcomes at fixed live-sized caps more reliably than extending the failed generic HYPE breakout route across assets.
decision: Select v23 for the next authorized live canary only after the active v14 generation completes a normal transition drain and venue reconciliation proves all positions and owned orders absent. V23 executes ETH pullback and SOL range onset in both directions, with no observer-only provider and no BTC or HYPE route. The selection authorizes a bounded empirical trial, not automatic economic promotion.
falsifier: Identity drift, incomplete v14 drain, inherited venue exposure, missing reduce-only stop protection, replay/live friction divergence, or ledger/TUI/config disagreement invalidates mechanical readiness. The economic hypothesis weakens if prospectively reconciled after-friction outcomes turn negative, either mechanism ceases contributing positively across independent outcomes, or SOL's sparse block evidence fails under continuous live sampling.
limitations: The final 60-day block was previously inspected and is descriptive rather than sealed holdout evidence.
SOL evidence is twelve measured blocks with gaps rather than continuous coverage.
One-minute bar replay cannot reproduce private queue position, every stop gap, or exact IOC slippage.
Realized-equity drawdown omits concurrent intratrade mark-to-market paths.
ETH's final short slice was slightly negative and requires explicit prospective monitoring.
Positive aggregate historical results do not establish durable live edge.
